semis.why: Day after a +4.3% SOX session (5th straight, 5d +12.5%, median +11.4% over 50d, AMD rsi73 / INTC rsi71 after the Meta Muse CPU rally) with sector volume only 1.02x normal outside the two leaders; Asia proxies sold into their close (Hynix -1.45%, TSMC TW -0.6%) while KOSPI/TAIEX held small gains; pre-market -0.9% (thin, no volume) led by AXTI -3.9 / AMD -1.4 with no scheduled catalyst before the Xi visit (Sep 23-25) and Meta Connect (Sep 23). Beyond the gap: the Asia intraday reversal in the memory/foundry proxies says the follow-through buyer is spent.

ai_power_infra.why: Scored on SOXX, so it inherits the semis give-back; the group itself is not stretched (median -1.1% vs 50d, pre +0.25%, Infineon +1.0) so hold, not trim.

big_tech.why: Rotation, not exit: pre-market bid is in the UN-stretched megacaps (MSFT +1.2, GOOG +0.6, AMZN +0.3, all within 8% of the 50d) while META (-0.7 pre, rsi78, +22% over 50d) gives back a little into Connect tomorrow; QQQ volume 1.42x on Monday = conviction. Beyond the +0.02% gap: the breadth of the bid inside big tech vs the fade inside chips, plus oil down five sessions and the 10Y off its high — a multiple tailwind for the long-duration names.

sg_banks.why: STI +0.98% today on bank leadership with UOB on 2.16x volume, DBS 1.33x (conviction at the SGX close); banks +3-5% over 50d, rsi ~60 = not stretched; Xi state visit from tomorrow is a China-sentiment tailwind for SG; ~21h horizon.

market.why: Macro support is real, not a cap: Nov WTI 92.37 -> 90.01 (-2.6% today, -7.7% over 5 sessions, same contract) and Brent Nov 100.34 -> 98.20 on Iran/Hormuz diplomacy headlines; 10Y eased 2bp to 4.94% off a two-decade high; VIX 14.7 in contango; megacap rotation absorbs the chip give-back. Beyond the +0.10% gap: falling oil + easing yields into a no-release session is the mechanism, not the gap. Corrects the 19:45 row, which treated an expiring-contract Brent print above $102 as a cap.

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have. Don't add to chipmakers or big tech today; the broad market and Singapore banks have a real tailwind from oil falling for a fifth straight session, so there is no reason to trim.
summary.where_we_are: 20:06 SGT / 08:06 ET, Tuesday. US pre-market, 84 minutes to the open; SGX closed at +0.98%. No scheduled US release before the close. Next events: Meta Connect and Xi Jinping's arrival in Washington, both Wednesday (Xi lands 4pm ET, ~4am SGT Thursday), Micron earnings Sep 30 (4:05am SGT Oct 1).
summary.macro_attribution: Oil has moved most: the November WTI contract fell from 92.37 to 90.01 (-2.6% today, -7.7% over five sessions, same contract compared with itself) and Brent November from 100.34 to 98.20, on reports Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days (CNBC, Sep 22). The 10-year yield eased 2bp to 4.94% and VIX sits at 14.7. The market and big-tech leans depend on this holding; press lines quoting Brent above $102 or WTI at $96 are the expiring October contract, not the live one.
what_happened: Chips rallied 4.3% Monday for a fifth straight gain, AMD +10% to a $1 trillion valuation and Intel +12%, on a CPU rush tied to Meta's Muse AI agent (Bloomberg, Sep 21). AMD and Intel now sit above RSI 70 and 24-25% over their 50-day average (tape). That is an extension, not a rebound.
The S&P 500 had its best day since early August (+1.5%) and the Nasdaq closed at a record (+2.3%) as oil and yields both slipped (CNBC, Sep 21). Futures are flat this morning (tape).

Oil reversed early gains after a Kyodo report that Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within seven days; Brent November -2.75% at $97.58 (CNBC, Sep 22). Five straight down sessions in front-month crude is a tailwind for the index, not a cap.

Asia sold the chip proxies into their close: SK Hynix -1.45% and TSMC Taiwan -0.6% while the KOSPI and TAIEX held small gains (tape). Chips are -0.9% pre-market, but Yahoo pre-market bars carry zero volume, so that print is thin.
Singapore banks led the STI up 0.98%, UOB on 2.16x normal volume and DBS on 1.33x (tape, SGX close). Real buying, and the Xi state visit from Wednesday is a China-sentiment tailwind for Singapore.

per_group.semis: Chipmakers slightly down. What the read adds beyond the -0.9% pre-market gap: the Asia intraday reversal says the follow-through buyer is spent. Pre-market volume is zero on Yahoo, so the gap itself is thin.
per_group.ai_power_infra: AI power (Bloom, Navitas, Infineon) slightly down, only because it is scored against the chip index. The group itself is not stretched (median 1% below its 50-day, Infineon +1% in Frankfurt), so hold rather than trim.
per_group.big_tech: Big tech slightly up. Rotation, not exit: the pre-market bid is in the un-stretched names (Microsoft +1.2%, Alphabet +0.6%, Amazon +0.3%, all within 8% of their 50-day) while Meta, up 22% over its 50-day, gives back a little into Connect. Beyond the flat gap: breadth of the bid inside big tech versus the fade inside chips, plus falling oil and easing yields as a multiple tailwind.
per_group.sg_banks: Singapore banks slightly up at Wednesday's close. Bank-led STI gain on heavy volume at today's close, RSI around 60 so not stretched, and the Xi visit sentiment tailwind.
per_group.market: Whole market slightly up. Front-month oil down five sessions, the 10-year off its two-decade high, VIX calm, and megacap rotation absorbing the chip give-back. This corrects the 19:45 read, which treated an expiring-contract Brent print above $102 as a cap on the upside.

change_my_mind: November WTI back above 92.37 (Monday's close) during the session removes the macro support and flips the whole-market lean to flat.
Chips opening more than 1.5% lower with big tech following them means contagion, not rotation, and flips big tech to flat.
The 10-year back above 5.00% puts the two-decade-high scare back on and turns every lean soft.
A late chip reversal to green on volume above 1.3x normal means the digestion call was wrong and the run is not done.
summary.confidence: the macro inputs (oil, 10-year, VIX) all point one way and are verified same-contract; the chip call is a digestion bet after five up days, which is near coin-flip on any single session.
summary.cant_know: Whether a single Iran headline reverses oil intraday, and whether the CPU-rotation buyers who chased AMD and Intel on Monday come back for a sixth day.
summary.the_call: Up, mildly. Expect the S&P a touch higher, under half a percent, with big tech leading on Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon. Chipmakers are the group that moves most and it is down: a moderate give-back led by AMD, Intel and AXT after five straight up days. Singapore banks move least, holding today's gain into Wednesday.
